lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 18 and in approved education
  - Child does not live with claimant
  - Claimant contributes £26.05/week towards child's upkeep (>= £26.05)
  - No one who lives with the child is already claiming
  - Child is not in local authority care

  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week

  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have a child or children you're responsible for?** If yes, please tell me:
- How many children do you have?
- What are their names?
- How old is each child?

This will help me guide you through the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child I'm responsible for. His name is Alex and he's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 18 years old.

Since Alex is 18 (which falls in the 16-19 age category), I need to check if he meets the additional requirements for this age group.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. For 16-19 year olds like Alex, eligibility depends on their education or training status. 

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In approved education or training** (such as full-time non-advanced education at school, college, or through an approved training program), OR
2. **Has he recently left education or training** (within the last 20 weeks)?

Please let me know which situation applies to Alex.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is currently in education. He's studying for his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is studying for his A-levels, which is relevant for Child Benefit eligibility. Let me check the education level requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! A-levels are considered approved non-advanced education for Child Benefit purposes. Now I need to check a few more details about Alex's education:

1. **Is Alex studying full-time?** (This means at least 12 hours per week of supervised study)

2. **Is his A-level course funded by an employer or linked to a job agreement with an employer?**

Please let me know the answers to these questions.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's studying full-time at college. And no, it's not funded by an employer - it's just regular college A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex's A-level course meets the education requirements. Now let me check the next criterion.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's work status:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week** (or not in paid work at all)?

For Child Benefit purposes, children aged 16+ who work 24 hours or more per week are not eligible, even if they're in education.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's just focused on his studies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is focused on his studies and not working. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Next question:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right**, such as:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit
- Or similar benefits?

Children who receive these benefits in their own right are not eligible for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue checking the eligibility criteria.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

If yes, please let me know:
- What type of apprenticeship (e.g., Foundation, Intermediate, Advanced, Higher, or Degree level)?
- Where in the UK is it (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

If Alex is not in an apprenticeship at all, just let me know that.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship. He's just doing his A-levels at college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Now let me move on to check your eligibility as the claimant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency status. To qualify for Child Benefit, you must meet UK residency requirements.

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

If not, please let me know if any of these apply to you:
- You have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You're living abroad as a Crown servant
- Other special circumstances

What's your residency situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You meet the residency requirement. Now let me check the responsibility requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex. You're considered responsible for a child if any of these apply:

1. **You live with Alex**, OR
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** (paying at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards their care - food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc.), OR
3. **You pay maintenance** under a court order or agreement

**Which of these applies to your situation with Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me, but I do contribute towards his upkeep. I help with things like clothes and other expenses.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying. You contribute to Alex's upkeep by helping with clothes and other expenses. Let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Important question: **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child at a time. For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Someone Alex lives with
- Another relative

Please let me know if:
- No one else is claiming for Alex, OR
- Someone else is claiming but you've agreed to transfer it to you, OR
- Someone else is claiming and there's a dispute about who should claim

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! No one else is claiming for Alex. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's living situation. **Is Alex currently:**

1. **In hospital** (for an extended period)?
2. **In local authority care** (looked after by the council)?
3. **Living with foster carers**?
4. **Living normally** (not in any of the above situations)?

Which situation applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is in hospital - he's been there for a while now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'm sorry to hear Alex is in hospital. For Child Benefit eligibility, the length of the hospital stay matters. Let me check the requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I need to understand Alex's hospital stay better. The rules about hospital stays can be complex:

**How long has Alex been in hospital?** 

Please note:
- Child Benefit can continue for up to 12 weeks while a child is in hospital
- If Alex has had multiple hospital stays, they may count together if the gaps between stays were less than 28 days
- The 12-week limit is cumulative across linked hospital stays

Can you tell me:
1. How many weeks Alex has been in hospital currently?
2. Has he had any other hospital stays recently (in the past few months)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in hospital for about 15 weeks now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Alex has been in hospital for about 15 weeks, which exceeds the 12-week threshold. Let me continue checking the requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
This is important: Even though Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, there's an exception to the rule.

**Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he is in hospital?**

This could include things like:
- Buying clothes, toiletries, or other personal items for him
- Providing pocket money
- Paying for things he needs while in hospital
- Other regular expenses for his benefit

If you or your partner (if you're married/in a civil partnership and living together) are regularly spending money on Alex, you may still be eligible for Child Benefit.

Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure - I haven't really been able to keep track of whether I've been spending money regularly on him or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - it can be difficult to keep track, especially during a stressful time like this. Let me ask this in a clearer way:

**Since Alex has been in hospital, have you been buying things for him or giving him money?** For example:
- Buying him clothes, toiletries, magazines, snacks, or entertainment items?
- Giving him pocket money or spending money?
- Paying for anything else he needs or wants?

Even if it's just occasional purchases or small amounts, it could count as "regularly spending" on him. 

Think about the last few weeks - have you spent any money on things for Alex, or do you visit him and bring him things he needs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I honestly can't say for certain whether I've been doing that regularly or not. I'm just not sure.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - this is a difficult situation and it's hard to be certain. Let me explain what this means for your eligibility assessment:

Since Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks (15 weeks), whether you can claim Child Benefit depends on whether you're regularly spending money on him. Because you're uncertain about this, I need to provide you with both possible outcomes:

**If you ARE regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital:**
- You may still be eligible for Child Benefit, and I would need to continue with a few more questions about his situation.

**If you are NOT regularly spending money on Alex:**
- Unfortunately, Child Benefit stops after 12 weeks in hospital if you're not regularly spending money on the child.

**My recommendation:** I suggest you:
1. Think carefully about any purchases, gifts, or money you've given to Alex in recent weeks
2. Check your bank statements or receipts if that helps
3. Contact HMRC directly on **0300 200 3100** to discuss your specific situation, as they can provide guidance based on the exact details

Would you like me to:
- **Continue the assessment** assuming you ARE regularly spending on Alex (to see if you'd be eligible in that scenario), OR
- **Provide you with the outcome** based on the uncertainty?

Which would be most helpful for you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I see. Well, to be honest, I really don't know whether I've been spending money on him regularly. I can't say for certain either way.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand - this is a challenging situation and you're being honest about the uncertainty. 

Given that this is a critical factor for your eligibility and you genuinely cannot determine whether you've been regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital, let me provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent

## Assessment Result: **INDETERMINATE** - Further Review Required

Based on our conversation, here's what I found:

### What's Working in Your Favor:
✓ Alex is 18 years old and in approved education (full-time A-levels)  
✓ He's not working 24+ hours per week  
✓ He's not receiving benefits in his own right  
✓ He's not in a disqualifying apprenticeship  
✓ You live in the UK (meeting residency requirements)  
✓ You contribute to Alex's upkeep  
✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex  

### The Complicating Factor:
⚠️ Alex has been in hospital for 15 weeks, which exceeds the standard 12-week limit. Child Benefit can continue beyond 12 weeks **IF** you are regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital. Since you're uncertain about whether you've been doing this regularly, I cannot make a definitive determination.

### What You Need to Do:
**Contact HMRC directly** to discuss your specific situation:
- **Child Benefit Helpline: 0300 200 3100**
- Lines are open Monday to Friday, 8am to 6pm

When you call, explain:
- Alex's hospital stay and duration
- Any spending you've done for Alex (even if irregular)
- Your uncertainty about the "regular spending" requirement

HMRC can review your specific circumstances, including looking at any evidence of spending (receipts, bank statements, etc.), and make a formal determination about your eligibility.

Is there anything else you'd like me to clarify about this assessment?
